content.value_statement: Email teams need test plans that separate signal from noise. This skill designs powered send experiments and reads results with clear promote, kill, or continue calls.
actual_capabilities: Selects A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out mode from the brief.
Creates falsifiable hypotheses and one-variable-per-cell variant matrices.
Estimates sample size, MDE, run duration, and power from baselines.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for email tests.
Reads ESP result exports and recommends promote, kill, or keep-testing.
Produces handoff summaries with assumptions, evidence labels, and next steps.
limitations: Requires user-provided baselines, list sizes, or exported results for useful calculations.
Does not write subject lines, body copy, or CTA text.
Does not compute a full EQS program score or veto decision.
Uses estimate tables when the optional local calculator is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Plan a Subject-Line A/B Test
use_cases.description: Build a two-cell email test with a clear hypothesis, metric choice, power plan, and read date.

use_cases.title: Design a Send-Time Experiment
use_cases.description: Compare send windows while holding subject, segment, and creative constant across randomized arms.

use_cases.title: Read Finished ESP Results
use_cases.description: Apply significance rules to delivered, open, click, or conversion counts and state the launch decision.

prompt_templates.title: Start an A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test for a retention email. Baseline open rate is 38 percent, list size is 12,000, and I want to detect a 3 point lift.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Send-Time Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a send-time experiment for a weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40 percent, list size is 20,000, and the goal is higher same-window engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multivariate Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a 2 by 2 subject and CTA test. Baseline click rate is 2.1 percent. Include sample size, duration, guardrails, and when to collapse to A/B.

prompt_templates.title: Read Out Test Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this finished test export with variant, delivered, opens, clicks, and conversions. Tell me if the winner is significant and whether to promote, kill, or keep testing.

output_examples.input: A retention list has 12,000 contacts, a 38 percent open baseline, and two subject-line concepts.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an A/B subject test with one control and one variant. It names open rate as the primary metric, estimates sample needs, and sets a fixed read date.

output_examples.input: A marketer wants to compare Tuesday morning, Thursday morning, and Sunday evening sends.
output_examples.output: The skill designs randomized send-time arms, keeps content constant, sets same-window engagement as the read metric, and warns about weekday mix.

output_examples.input: An ESP export shows delivered counts, clicks, and conversions for control and variant arms.
output_examples.output: The skill names the significance method, reports whether the result clears the practical lift gate, and gives a promote, kill, or keep-testing decision.

best_practices: Provide baseline rates, list size, send volume, and the smallest lift worth acting on.
Change one variable per test cell so the result has a clear cause.
Use a fixed sample size and read date before reviewing results.
anti_patterns: Do not test subject, CTA, and creative changes in one A/B cell.
Do not call a winner before the planned sample and read date.
Do not promote a result that fails guardrails such as complaints or unsubscribes.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs the test goal, baseline metric, list size, send volume, and minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: Can it analyze a completed test?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide delivered counts and outcome counts for each arm from your ESP or analytics export.

faq.question: Does it write the email creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and read-out. Use a creative skill for subject lines, body copy, or CTAs.

faq.question: Does it support hold-out testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan send versus no-send controls and size the test on conversion or revenue outcomes.

faq.question: How does it handle small lists?
faq.answer: It explains when the list is underpowered and recommends a larger effect, fewer cells, or a longer run.

faq.question: Can it use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible hosts.
